chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:

He (the Imam) said: 'He will not enter Paradise whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance.' I said, 'So I said, 'We are from Allah and to Him we are returning' (Istirja'). He said: 'What is the matter with you saying Istirja'?' I said, 'Because of what I heard from you.' He said: 'It is not where you are going (understanding it). Rather, I mean the rejection (of Wilayah). Rather, it (arrogance) is the rejection (of Wilayah).'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific meaning of arrogance (kibr) that prevents entry into Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'arrogance' barring entry to Paradise is not merely general pride, but specifically 'al-jahud' (denial/rejection), particularly of Wilayah. The narrator’s initial reaction of 'Istirja'' (returning to God) upon hearing the severe warning highlights the gravity of this specific theological denial, distinguishing it from common social pride.
